detailedExplanation: This topic is verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Biology Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and the corresponding AQA GCSE Biology 8461 content.

Photosynthesis is an endothermic process because energy is transferred from the environment by light and absorbed by chlorophyll. In plant and algal cells, chloroplasts contain chlorophyll which absorbs light energy. That energy is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose, with oxygen released as a product.
Photosynthesis provides chemical energy and carbon-containing molecules that underpin most food chains.

additionalSourceSections.heading: Core Equation
additionalSourceSections.body:
Photosynthesis word equation:
carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen

Symbol equation:
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

Light energy is absorbed by chlorophyll in chloroplasts; photosynthesis is endothermic because energy is transferred from the environment.
